corpus_before.name: Suppression of the Indigenous La Gomera revolt after the killing of Hernán Peraza, date unresolved
corpus_before.date_numeric_proxy_basis: nearest reviewed parent midpoint used only as a model coordinate: atlas-canary-islands
corpus_before.date_resolution: Mitchell's island table assigns La Gomera a conquest date of 1489, while Espino's punitive-repression sequence places Pedro de Vera's replacement in 1488 after the described operations; neither direct passage gives an explicit date for the revolt and punishment themselves. Because these markers appear to concern different scopes and do not establish one event year, both fields remain UNKNOWN.
corpus_before.mechanism: Punitive expedition after Peraza's killing; encirclement and defeat; executions, dismemberment, mutilation, drowning, enslavement, sale, and deterrent terror directed beyond the identified killers
agents: Hernán Peraza as the seigneur whose intervention in Indigenous factional conflict and killing preceded the punishment; his widow Beatriz de Bobadilla; Gran Canaria governor Pedro de Vera and a force of four hundred men; the Indigenous Pala and Mulagua factions
victims: Gomeros of the Pala and Mulagua factions besieged at Garajonay; people executed or mutilated; minors, children, and women enslaved or sold; and Gomeros living at Telde and Gáldar who were arrested and killed. Complete counts and individual affiliations remain unresolved.
corpus_before.summary: The sources directly establish one island-specific punitive episode and multiple territorial-removal mechanisms even though its date and property outcomes remain unresolved. El Hierro and Gran Canaria processes are excluded rather than combined with it.
corpus_before.disputes: The source does not provide a parcel-by-parcel Indigenous ownership record, a beneficiary roster for the territorial distributions, or complete victim and captive counts. Those values remain unknown and no tract-level dispossession count is inferred.
corpus_before.event_json_summary: Punitive military defeat followed by execution, enslavement, sale, and forced removal of Gomero residents

sources.title: Peter J. Mitchell, Archaeological Research in the Canary Islands: Island Archaeology off Africa's Atlantic Coast; Antonio Espino López, Granada, Canarias, América: el uso de prácticas aterrorizantes en la praxis de tres conquistas, 1482–1557; Manuel Lobo Cabrera, Formas de poder y economía canaria entre los siglos XV–XVII
sources.locator: Historia de Hermigua > Edad Moderna, paragraphs 1-6 (web text lines 4-9)

corpus_before.parent_overlap_ruling: The input's El Hierro–La Gomera composite is not one event: El Hierro's early Norman and later seigneurial control is separated from the much later La Gomera revolt and punitive expedition by actors, population, island, and chronology. The revised target contains only the directly documented La Gomera repression and remains distinct from Pedro de Vera's Gran Canaria conquest because its trigger and affected population are Gomero.

corpus_before.name: Israeli settlement advancement and associated Palestinian land-control mechanisms in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem (2023–2024 evidence window)
corpus_before.date_numeric_proxy_basis: known end used only as a model coordinate; onset year remains unresolved
corpus_before.date_resolution: A/HRC/58/73 covers 1 November 2023 through 31 October 2024 and describes settlement transfer, maintenance, and expansion as ongoing. The cited paragraphs do not state the historical start or completion of the wider system, so the start year remains UNKNOWN and 2024 is an evidence cutoff rather than an end finding.
corpus_before.mechanism: Transfer of administrative and legal powers from military to civilian government; settlement planning and approval; outpost regularization; infrastructure development; land designation, seizure, and allocation; state-land declarations; discriminatory construction enforcement; and settlement and housing-plan expansion that fragments Palestinian territory
agents: Government of Israel; civilian officials including the Additional Minister and Settlement Administration; the Israeli military commander and Civil Administration; Israeli settlers
victims: Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, affected by land seizures, discriminatory planning and building enforcement, coercive transfer pressures, and territorial fragmentation; Israeli civilians transferred to or maintained in settlements; exact household membership is not established
corpus_before.summary: The opened report identifies one West Bank and East Jerusalem settlement-administration system with direct land-control mechanisms and effects on Palestinian territory. It excludes the Golan and does not infer household membership; a fresh profile is required because the wrapper mixed distinct territories.
corpus_before.disputes: The report supports all domains for its evidence window but leaves the wider system's historical start, parcel and household membership, individual outcomes, and post-31-October-2024 developments unresolved.
corpus_before.event_json_summary: Settlement planning and expansion, land designation and seizure, administrative transfer, discriminatory enforcement, and Palestinian territorial fragmentation

sources.title: United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, A/HRC/58/73, Israeli settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan
sources.locator: The UN endpoint resolved to the official A/HRC/58/73 body despite returning DOCX rather than PDF, and paragraphs 2-5 and 8-15 were present and usable at the stated locator.

corpus_before.parent_overlap_ruling: Distinct territorial child of atlas-israeli-settlements-opt: limited to the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Palestinian population-land relationship there; excludes the occupied Syrian Golan and the Gaza resettlement discussion outside the cited paragraph range.
